title: The Motorola Razr Fold has an accessory problem that no one’s talking about
summary: A scratched screen is inevitable for the Razr Fold.
body: Foldable phones are fragile. That’s what a lot of people think, and while I don’t think foldables are as delicate as their reputation implies, you should protect a folding phone in the same way you would any other. I hate display scratches, even minor ones, so I always use a screen protector and a case with every phone I have. Then I got the Motorola Razr Fold , and that changed. Not because it’s a phone that doesn’t need screen protectors, but because it’s almost impossible to find quality accessories for the phone.

title: The Pixel 10 Pro is a flawed and inconsistent phone — and I’m still using it one year later
summary: The Pixel 10 Pro is flawed but lovable.
body: I find it hard to believe that it’s been almost a year since I got my Pixel 10 Pro . Since August 28th, it has been my primary phone (almost) every day, and I adore this phone when it’s working as it should. The problem, as is often the case with Pixels, is that it doesn’t always work as Google intended. Looking back, it’s been a year of ups and downs with the Pixel 10 Pro, but it’s still the only phone I want to call my own.

title: A Snapdragon-powered Pixel might sound amazing. Here’s why it’s a terrible idea
summary: Do you really wanna pay a lot more money for your Pixel flagship?
body: Credit: David Imel / Android Authority It’s been roughly five years since Google first dropped Snapdragon silicon in Pixel phones in favor of its Tensor processors. I think it’s fair to say this move has been a double-edged sword for the company. Sure, there’s been good everyday performance, capable on-device AI, and great camera capabilities. But the transition also brought modem issues, heating problems, and uncompetitive peak performance. This state of affairs has led enthusiasts to urge Google to return to Snapdragon silicon, and it seems like an intriguing idea at first. But the more I thought about this possibility, the more I realized this probably wouldn’t be a great move for Pixel phones.

title: Joe Jonas Says He Sought Therapy After His Solo Album Underperformed
summary: Fastlife peaked at No. 15 on the Billboard 200, while its lead single "See No More" reached No. 92 on the Hot 100.
body: Joe Jonas has revealed that the disappointing commercial performance of his 2011 solo debut Fastlife triggered panic attacks and physical pain that ultimately led him to seek therapy. The singer reflected on the album’s reception during a recent episode of the Hey Jonas! podcast, which he co-hosts with his Jonas Brothers bandmates and siblings, Nick and Kevin Jonas. Jonas said he had expected the record to match the success the trio had enjoyed at their peak and had tied its outcome to his own self-worth. “Somewhere in my core, I was like, ‘If I do that, then I matter,'” he told his brothers. Fastlife peaked at No. 15 on the Billboard 200, while its lead single “See No More” reached No. 92 on the Hot 100 — results Jonas found deeply deflating. “I started having panic attacks and started having physical pain,” he recalled. He said a doctor found him physically healthy and recommended he see a therapist, a suggestion he initially resisted. “I was like, what do you mean a therapist? I don’t need a therapist. Why would I need a therapist?” he said, adding that he instead took long bike rides to get away from his phone. …

The Yolŋu rapper won Album of the Year for DJANDJAY , while his single “THICK SKIN” — featuring Thelma Plum, Emma Donovan, Kee’ahn and Jada Weazel — claimed both Song of the Year and Film Clip of the Year. Baker Boy performed the track live at the ceremony, bringing out Donovan as a surprise guest. Cousin duo Birdz and Fred Leone won Artist of the Year, their first NIMA, on the strength of their debut EP GIRA . Drifting Clouds took Best New Talent, Northern Peninsula Area won Community Clip of the Year for “All The Way From The NPA,” and Bulman School & Community earned the Indigenous Language Award for “LOK LOK MAH BURARR” (Lizard & Goanna). As previously announced, blues musician Marlene Cummins and Elcho Island’s Saltwater Band were inducted into the NIMAs Hall of Fame, with the night closing on a tribute to the band. “Last night’s celebration brought together some of the most incredible music and musicians this country…

body: Seoul was already deep in the heat of August when thousands of MYs made their way to Gocheok Sky Dome for the opening weekend of aespa ‘s fourth world tour. Across Aug. 7 and 8, Karina, Winter, Giselle and Ningning welcomed a combined 35,000 fans to aespa’s first concerts at the dome, opening SYNK : COMPLæXITY with 27 songs across roughly two-and-a-half hours. Built around “CRACK,” a rupture that brings aespa into conflict with altered versions of ae-aespa, the show unfolds through five chapters: singularity, intrusion, confinement, awakening and resolution. title: Google is making it easier to add new sources to Gemini Notebook
summary: You may not see the new feature right away.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Google is rolling out an update for Gemini Notebooks. An “Add a source to Gemini Notebook” step has been added to automate adding sources. This feature is available for Business, Enterprise, and Education customers. Earlier this year, Google rolled out automatic Drive syncing to Gemini Notebooks. The change made it much easier to keep your sources up-to-date. Another source-related change is now rolling out to Notebooks. This change aims to take the burden out of adding sources. In a blog post , Google announced it’s pushing out an update to Gemini Notebooks. The update will add a new “Add a source to Gemini Notebook” step that automates adding new sources. With this new feature, you’ll be able to add text, links to Drive files, or generic YouTube or web URLs as sources. Before this step was rolled out, users had to manually add sources one by one.

title: Google Photos users report handy drag-to-select feature has disappeared
summary: A popular Google Photos feature has gone M.I.A. for some
body: Credit: Taylor Kerns / Android Authority TL;DR Google Photos users are reporting that a feature has suddenly gone missing. The affected users can no longer drag to select multiple photos. This problem has been spotted on Pixel, Galaxy, and OnePlus phones. Recently, Google Photos users have noticed that the app won’t let them search for terms related to regulated or illicit substances . While that appears to be an intentional choice implemented into Google’s guardrails, a new issue has popped up that seems unintentional. A convenient photo selection feature has suddenly disappeared from the app for some. Google Photos users are flocking to Reddit to report that drag to select no longer works for them. If you’re unfamiliar with drag to select, the feature allows you to select multiple photos by dragging your finger across the screen. It works by long-pressing a photo to enable multi-select. Once enabled, you can drag your finger to select all the photos you want.

title: I gave my Samsung phone superpowers with a $6 pack of NFC tags — here’s how
summary: Cheap NFC tags and Samsung Routines do more than you think.
body: NFC is a smartphone feature that isn’t nearly as appreciated as it should be. It’s not as flashy as UWB nor as integral as Wi-Fi, but NFC powers some of the simplest tools that help me plow through the mundanities of the day. A few months ago, I picked up a bunch of NFC tags for a specific Android Auto automation project I was working on. I needed just two tags for that, so needless to say, I had plenty of spare chips that needed a purpose. And boy, have I found perfect uses for them!

title: I’m finally streaming Netflix in 4K on Chrome — here’s how you can too
summary: I pixel-peeped so you don't have to.
body: If you use Chrome , you probably know how frustratingly difficult it is to watch Netflix in 4K. Despite paying for the Premium plan, I’ve always had to switch to Microsoft Edge on my Windows PC or Safari on my MacBook just to get the best streaming quality. And when Chrome is the browser I use for practically everything, switching browsers just for Netflix gets annoying very quickly. So, when I heard Netflix was finally bringing 4K streaming to Chrome , I genuinely jumped with joy. I’m not kidding or exaggerating — that was my exact reaction. Unfortunately, my excitement didn’t last very long.

title: Just got your Galaxy Z Fold 8? Here are the first 5 things you need to do
summary: I love the Fold 8, but it's not perfect out of the box.
body: I’m currently using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 , and it doesn’t take long to realize it’s a special device. I loved my Microsoft Surface Duo, original Google Pixel Fold, and BlackBerry Passport — all phones with one thing in common: a wider aspect ratio. We’ve been stuck in an era of taller, narrower devices for the last decade or so, and the few phones that slip through that offer a different experience, I’m all over. If you’re like me and excited to get your hands on the Galaxy Z Fold 8, there are some important steps you should go through when first starting out — especially if you’ve only used traditional slab smartphones or even other book-style foldables. Here are the five things I recommend doing first once you pick up your Galaxy Z Fold 8.

title: Before you buy another USB-C charger, make sure it has this critical (and hidden) spec
summary: Buying a USB-C charger is still harder than it should be.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority Buying the perfect USB-C charger may look simple at first, but the reality is full of potential gotchas. If you’ve ever reached for your cable only to find that your device is still charging hours later, you’re certainly not alone. In one sense, USB-C and USB Power Delivery were supposed to solve this mess. The universal connector and new regulations, such as those introduced in the EU, were designed to ensure that one charger could support everything. In some ways, that has been a success: USB-C can now be found on almost every phone, tablet, laptop, and more. However, the difference between something that technically works and something that works optimally can still be surprisingly wide.

title: Vera Blue covers Radiohead’s ‘Creep’ for triple j’s Like A Version
summary: Blue also performed "Maze," a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals.
body: Vera Blue has taken on one of alternative rock’s most enduring songs, covering Radiohead ‘s “Creep” for triple j’s Like A Version . The Australian singer-songwriter stripped the 1992 track back to three elements — electric guitar, piano and vocals — building from the lower end of her range into a soaring falsetto by the chorus. Late in the performance she deployed The Pipe, a mouth-controlled dynamic effects processor and synthesizer made by SOMA Laboratory, adding an eerie texture to the arrangement. Blue said she was drawn to the song’s emotional core, describing “Creep” as an “epic rock song” whose lyrics are also “heartbreaking,” and aiming for a “very haunting version” that still nods to Thom Yorke’s original. Blue also performed “Maze,” a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals , during her studio session. The album is due Friday, Aug. 21 via Island Records/Universal Music Australia, and Blue will support it with a national tour opening the same night at Brisbane’s Princess Theatre and running through Perth’s The Rechabite on Aug. 28. summary: ESPN Unlimited was promised last fall, and now it's beginning to arrive.
body: TL;DR In the fallout from last year’s Disney/YouTube TV spat, subscribers were promised free ESPN Unlimited. YTTV users are now starting to be notified about the arrival of their ESPN Unlimited perks. Initial access is through the ESPN app, with YTTV streaming arriving later. Last fall, Google and Disney found themselves butting heads over YouTube TV carriage agreements , with subscribers temporarily losing access to multiple ABC, ESPN, and National Geographic channels. It was embarrassing to see the corporate spat played out in public like it was, with YTTV subscribers effectively turned into bargaining chips. When they inevitably sorted things out, viewers were issued a credit , and Google announced a new deal that would, among things, bring a new ESPN offering to YTTV. And now, the better part of a year later, that’s finally happening. We just got this email notifying us of ESPN Unlimited arriving for YouTube TV accounts:

title: Leak spills the beans on the Sony WH-1000XM4 revival
summary: Sony is reportedly resurrecting the classic noise-canceling headphones under a new name.
body: TL;DR A new leak has spilled the beans on Sony’s upcoming WH-1000XM4C headphones, a spinoff of the now-discontinued WH-1000XM4. These headphones will reportedly retain a bulk of the hardware used in the original, but with a shorter battery life. title: Google Messages makes one-handed use much easier with new rollout
summary: The new, redesigned floating context menu and selective text copying make messaging on large phones less frustrating.
body: Credit: Sanuj Bhatia / Android Authority TL;DR Google Messages is expanding its server-side rollout of the floating context menu and selective text copying to more beta users. The redesigned floating menu places actions like Reply, Copy, Edit, Star, and Delete in a clean vertical list right by the text bubble for easier one-handed use. Selective text copying introduces draggable handles, allowing users to highlight specific details without copying an entire message. Google Messages finally appears to be expanding a major usability refresh to more users, bringing its redesigned floating context menu and selective text copying to (slightly) wider availability. Reddit user seeareeff reports that they could finally see the new floating context menu when long-pressing a message bubble. Rather than dumping action icons into the top action bar (which forced awkward hand re-gripping on larger phones), the vertical floating menu appears right below/above the text. Essential actions like Reply, Copy, Edit, Star, and Delete are neatly grouped in a clean list format that makes one-handed interaction far less frustrating.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the wrong Samsung foldable to buy this year
summary: It's giving middle-child energy.
body: Samsung gave us two very different foldables this year: the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra . Both these foldables are aimed at completely different people. The Fold 8 introduces a new direction for Samsung with a wider display, a thinner chassis, and a much more compact feel in the hand. Meanwhile, the Fold 8 Ultra carries forward what the Galaxy Z Fold 7 started, refining that familiar formula. Here’s the thing, though: you’d expect two completely different form factors to come with equally different feature sets. Instead, they’re remarkably similar, and the Fold 8 Ultra is priced just $200 more than the Fold 8. That’s exactly what got me thinking. For such a relatively small price increase, the Ultra offers enough extra value that it almost feels like Samsung is nudging buyers in that direction.

title: The OnePlus 15 and 15R just got ColorOS beta
summary: The update, likely based on Android 17, is currently open to OnePlus 15 series in India.
body: TL;DR OnePlus has opened the first global ColorOS closed beta for the OnePlus 15 and 15R. The testing program is currently limited to Indian variants and excludes US, EU, and global models. OnePlus hasn’t confirmed the wider rollout yet. OnePlus has officially begun its transition from OxygenOS to ColorOS , opening the first global Closed Beta Testing (CBT) program for the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus 15R. If you’ve been wondering when the software migration announced alongside the company’s withdrawal from the US and European smartphone markets would actually begin, this is the clearest sign yet that it’s now underway. There’s one important catch, though. While both the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus 15R are available in the US, the inaugural ColorOS beta is currently reserved exclusively for Indian variants of the two phones. There’s no mention of the base OS, but Android 17 is expected, given that OnePlus has been testing the OS on the OnePlus 15 since March .

title: Samsung’s latest 200MP sensor could be a fantastic upgrade for Galaxy S27 Ultra
summary: This new sensor could be just what Samsung's flagships need in the wake of LOFIC-equipped camera sensors.
body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has announced the ISOCELL HPC 200MP camera sensor for smartphones. This sensor brings a new pixel structure that enables dramatically improved dynamic range, reduced noise, and more. This would be a significant improvement over the 200MP sensor currently used on Samsung’s Ultra phones. Samsung debuted the first 200MP smartphone camera sensor back in 2022, and it has offered a variety of 200MP sensors since then. The pixels on these sensors are tiny, though, which isn’t great for image quality. However, the company’s latest 200MP camera sensor brings an interesting solution. Samsung has quietly announced the ISOCELL HPC camera sensor (thanks, Dylan H!). At first glance, this 200MP sensor has a lot in common with the ISOCELL HP2 used on the Galaxy S26 Ultra and its predecessors. That means a 1/1.3-inch sensor, 0.6-micron pixels, and Super Quad Phase-Detection autofocus.

title: Android’s new Quick Settings editor has another trick: A customizable QQS layout
summary: A handy tweak for anyone who frequently controls music or podcasts from the notification shade.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s latest Android Canary build includes another Quick Settings customization option that wasn’t highlighted initially. Users can also place the media player above Quick Quick Settings, changing what appears after the first swipe down. Just hours after Google rolled out the latest Android Canary 2608 build with its new Quick Settings layout editor , Google’s Mishaal Rahman has highlighted another neat customization option that didn’t make the initial announcement.

title: August’s Android Canary release gets app handles and new Quick Settings layout editor
summary: Sadly, it's also the end of the line for Pixel 6 phones.
body: TL;DR Google’s latest Android Canary build is now out, supporting Pixel 6 and newer hardware. This will be the final Android Canary release for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro. Today’s 2608 build introduces some new ways to customize Quick Settings. Google’s got tons of options right now for testers looking to get a taste of Android’s latest changes before anybody else, but you absolutely need to be first in line, there’s no better option than the Android Canary program. It’s been exactly one month since the 2607 July build arrived, and Google is now back with August’s Android Canary 2608. Over on Reddit’s Canary sub, Google shares the news of Android Canary 2608’s availability. Sadly, it’s not all good, and we’ve got some bad news for testers hoping to eke a little more life out of some of Google’s oldest hardware: Just like Android 17 QPR2 , Canary is also dropping support for the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro . The good news is that you can still install today’s release — but that’s it; you’re cut off, going forward.

title: GrapheneOS isn’t pulling any punches in its beef with Revolut
summary: The gloves are off as GrapheneOS calls Revolut's approach to security "incredibly negligent."
body: Credit: Calvin Wankhede / Android Authority TL;DR GrapheneOS says some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app. The project claims Revolut is specifically targeting GrapheneOS while still supporting outdated Android versions. GrapheneOS suggests a possible workaround but warns that it may not continue to work in the long term. Banking apps can be suspicious of anything that strays from the standard Android experience, but GrapheneOS clearly believes Revolut is taking that distrust way too far. The privacy-focused Android project claims some users are once again having trouble logging into the Revolut app, accusing the fintech company of deliberately trying to shut them out. In a thread on X , GrapheneOS said Revolut is blaming the restriction on security concerns, but argued that the real issue is that they’re enforcing licensing on Google Play . It also questioned how strict Revolut’s security standards can really be when the app still supports Android 9, which launched back in 2018. It went further, describing Revolut as “incredibly negligent when it comes to security.”

title: Next week’s Pixel 11 launch has found its host — and a whole lot of guest stars
summary: Pixel 11 launch dials up celebrity power with Trevor Noah, Stephen Curry, and more.
body: TL;DR Google’s Pixel 11 launch event is coming up next Wednesday, August 12. Today Google confirms that comedian Trevor Noah will be performing hosting duties. Noah is to be joined by past Google guests like Stephen Curry, as well as a bunch of new ones. With less than a week to go until August 12 , we are in full Pixel 11 anticipation mode, looking forward to all the hardware getting set to debut at the next Made by Google event. Lately, we’ve been captivated not just by Pixel 11 leak after Pixel 11 leak , but also Google starting to whet our appetite with a few official teasers . Today it takes those to the next level with a look at not just what , but who we can look forward to at the event itself. As you may remember from last summer, Jimmy Fallon hosted the Pixel 10 launch , joined by celebs like the NBA’s Stephen Curry, Formula 1’s Lando Norris, and the Jonas Brothers. And for the Pixel 11 launch, Google sure looks like its getting ready to turn that celebrity dial up to 11.

title: Maybe the FCC was onto something: These routers are phoning home to China with a secret backdoor
summary: Of course, because they predate the ban, the FCC continues to permit their sale.
body: TL;DR A new report details a massive security flaw in Zbtlink-made routers. The routers are programmed to ping a hard-coded list of servers, traced back to China. Once connected, the routers grant full root access — no authentication required. This past spring, the FCC announced a sweeping ban on new foreign-made routers — like the kind you use to get online with your ISP and connect all your devices to Wi-Fi. This was all done in the name of national security, but just how real of a threat do routers pose? The discovery of a new security vulnerability in some Chinese-made routers may have you looking at the FCC’s action in a slightly more sympathetic light. Jacob Baines at VulnCheck shares his analysis of routers made by Zbtlink, sold under both that and Wiflyer branding. While neither are huge names in the router space, they’re still sold through US retailers like Amazon , and have been around for years — so, plenty of time for these devices to make some inroads on the market.

title: Best Ring Floodlight Cam deal yet brings it down to $149.99
summary: The 2nd-gen Ring Floodlight Cam Wired is 25% off at Amazon, down to $149.99 with 2K video, two-way talk, and a siren.
body: Amazon has cut $50 off the newest Ring Floodlight Cam Wired, bringing it down to $149.99 from its $199.99 RRP. That is a 25% discount relative to the recommended retail price, and it is the first time Amazon has discounted this product, so this is a good moment to grab it. See the deal at Amazon

title: Here’s our best look yet at the Galaxy S26 FE
summary: Leaked images offer an early look at Samsung’s upcoming mid-tier flagship in three colors.
body: TL;DR The Samsung Galaxy S26 FE has just appeared in a series of images, revealing three color options. Among the major visual differences from the Galaxy S25 FE is the rear camera setup, which now resembles that of the Galaxy S26. Samsung hasn’t set a date for the phone’s launch, but a company executive recently confirmed it’s on the way. Following the launch of Samsung’s latest range of foldables, the focus now shifts to the company’s next smartphone, the Galaxy S26 FE. The mid-tier flagship has already appeared on multiple occasions, including in a case leak just this week . We’re now being treated to a series of official-looking images detailing the Galaxy S26 FE, giving us our best look yet of the smartphone. A total of three new images have been revealed by the folks at Android Headlines , showing the device in three colors: blue, black, and light green. The blue model we’re seeing here doesn’t look too dissimilar to the Galaxy S25 FE in the Navy colorway (as you can see up top).

title: Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones are 42% off in this open-box deal
summary: The deal cuts the flagship ANC headphones to $229 open-box, far below new pricing and packed with premium features.
body: The Sony WH-1000XM6 open-box deal at Focus cuts a big chunk off Sony’s flagship headphone price right now. You can get them for $229, down from the $398 RRP, which is a $169 saving and a 42% discount relative to the recommended retail price. See the deal at Focus That price stands out even more because buying new has not been cheaper than $378, and often more. For anyone who has been waiting for a real drop on the WH-1000XM6, this is the kind of gap that makes the open-box route worth a close look.

title: Google Search patches bug that broke time filters
summary: The widespread bug that ignored selected date ranges has now been resolved.
body: TL;DR Google has fixed the Search time filter bug that ignored selected date ranges. A Google Search VP confirmed the fix shipped earlier this week. If time filters are still broken, Google is asking users to report it. Good news for anyone who spent the past few days struggling to find recent news or software updates: Google has finally fixed its broken Search time filter feature. We recently reported that Google Search’s time filters — such as “Past 24 hours,” “Past month,” or custom date ranges — had stopped working globally. Instead of isolating results to your chosen timeframe, Search returned a random mix of old and new content, forcing users to rely on manual search operators as a workaround.

title: AYANEO’s new Game Boy Advance clone is more affordable than expected
summary: The handheld starts at just $89.
body: TL;DR AYANEO’s Game Boy Advance-inspired KONKR Pocket Advance is available to preorder now, starting at $89. The handheld is powered by MediaTek’s Helio G90T, the same chip found in the AYANEO Pocket Air Mini. The Pocket Advance boasts a 3.5-inch 960×640 display, a 4,000mAh battery, Android 12, active cooling, and more. If you’ve been waiting for AYANEO’s latest Android handheld to finally arrive, now’s the time to get your wallet ready. Oh, and the good news is that your wallet won’t be getting much lighter than previously expected! AYANEO’s Game Boy Advance (GBA) clone, which was first teased early in July , is finally available to pre-order. It’s called the KONKR Pocket Advance , and we finally have in-depth information about it.

title: Google Wallet now lets kids tap to pay without giving up parental control
summary: Your child gets tap to pay, but not a free pass to overspend.
body: TL;DR Google Wallet now supports supervised balances for kids and teens under 18 in the US, giving them a way to make digital payments with parental oversight. Parents can set daily spending limits, view transaction history, receive Family Link purchase alerts, and remotely lock the Wallet if a device is lost. Kids can tap to pay using their Android phone or Wear OS smartwatch anywhere Google Pay is accepted. Giving kids money has always involved a bit of trust. Maybe it’s cash for a weekend outing, a card for an emergency, or money to grab something while they’re out with friends. The problem is that cash is easy to lose, cards can go missing, and it’s not always obvious where the money ended up. That’s exactly the problem Google Wallet is now trying to solve. The company is rolling out supervised Google Wallet balances for children and teenagers under 18 in the US. Instead of handing your child a debit card and simply hoping they spend responsibly, you’ll be able to decide how much money they have access to while still keeping an eye on where it’s going. It’s a much more practical way to let kids start managing their own money without throwing them in at the deep end.

title: Mysterious new Garmin smartwatch spotted in FCC filings
summary: The unannounced device offers LTE and satellite connectivity.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR A new Garmin smartwatch has been spotted in an FCC filing. The device carries the model number A05170 and has support for LTE and satellite connectivity. It also features 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, Bluetooth Low Energy, ANT/ANT+, and NFC. Now that the Cirqa Smart Band is out, you may be wondering what else Garmin is working on. This will come as a surprise, but it turns out that the company’s next product will be a smartwatch. I know, I know, no one could’ve seen that coming. This smartwatch was recently spotted in a regulatory filing. The folks over at Gadgets and Wearables found the filing sitting in the FCC’s database. These documents don’t include the name of the device, but they do reveal that the model number is A05170. Additionally, Garmin describes the hardware as a portable digital transceiver, but the SAR evaluation report calls it a wrist-worn device.

title: Survey confirms your Fold 8 preference aligns with Samsung pre-orders
summary: We need more square phones.
body: Samsung’s latest foldable lineup is a departure from what the company’s been doing up to now. Rather than the usual two foldables — a Flip and a Fold — Samsung’s released three, including two book-style Z Fold phones in different aspect ratios. People have seemed excited about the new, wider form factor (the marginally less premium of the two) since before the phones were released , and now a survey Android Authority ‘s been running has confirmed that vibe. In a poll we’ve been running since late July, we asked readers which of the two Z Fold 8 phones they’d be more likely to buy. There were four options: the wide Z Fold 8; the narrow, higher-end Z Fold 8 Ultra; a response for people who hadn’t decided yet; and one for folks who just aren’t interested. After more than 1,000 responses, the wide Z Fold 8 ran away with it, nabbing nearly 60% of all votes.

title: Did the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra’s crease get worse after a couple of weeks?
summary: A tipster says the Z Fold 8 Ultra's crease has gotten worse over time. But has it?
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR A tipster has posted an image comparing the creases on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and OPPO Find N6. The tipster claimed that the Z Fold 8 Ultra’s crease got worse after less than two weeks of use. We can also confirm that the Ultra phone’s crease is more pronounced, but that it still feels the same. Samsung’s new foldable phones generally have less prominent creases than their predecessors, bringing us a little closer to a zero-crease future. However, at least one Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra owner reports that the crease has become more visible after mere days. Tipster @sondesix posted a picture comparing the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra to the OPPO Find N6 (h/t: PhoneArena ). The user later remarked that the Z Fold 8 Ultra’s crease became more prominent after just under two weeks of usage. The image does suggest that the Samsung phone has a more noticeable crinkle.

title: I’m glad Google is making the Pixel Tag, but I absolutely won’t buy one
summary: The Pixel Tag won't tempt split Apple and Google households like mine.
body: Apple is excellent at building product ecosystems — it’s ready to sell you almost everything you need for your iPhone, from AirPods to AirTags. Comparatively, Google has been slower to expand its Pixel hardware lineup. There are still glaring holes in the Pixel portfolio, including over-ear headphones and Bluetooth trackers. However, Google might be filling the latter hole with the Pixel Tag, a Bluetooth tracker built for the Google Find Hub network . It’ll be the perfect Android alternative to the AirTag and Apple’s Find My network… or will it?

title: Nothing is literally doubling down on its smartphone ambitions, contrary to previous report
summary: Nothing suggests it will launch up to six phones in 2027, doubling the total number of phones it released this year.
body: TL;DR Nothing co-founder Akis Evangelidis has revealed that the company may launch twice as many phones in 2027 as it did this year. The executive also reiterated that the US market is a “major priority” for Nothing in the audio segment. Nothing seems to have more products planned for launch this quarter, though Evangelidis didn’t specify if they were phones or other devices. Nothing has largely succeeded in capturing the tech industry’s imagination despite being a relatively new entrant. Following the Phone 1, the company has released multiple flagships, including the Phone 4a Pro earlier this year . We’re now getting an early glimpse of the company’s ambitious plans for 2027, even as the tech world struggles with the RAM crisis. In an interview with Times Now Tech , Nothing co-founder Akis Evangelidis revealed the company plans to launch twice as many phones in 2027 as it did this year. If our math is accurate, this could potentially mean the release of up to six Nothing devices next year. For reference, Nothing has released three smartphones in 2026, including the vanilla Phone 4a, the Phone 4a Pro, and the Phone 4b . “We’ll share more details closer to launch, but the idea is …

title: Forget cheap TVs, this upcoming Roku TV projector could be yours for less than $70
summary: Aurzen's budget Roku TV projector comes with a preorder deal that's too hard to ignore.
body: Credit: Aurzen TL;DR Aurzen will launch a mini portable smart projector with Roku TV next month. The projector will be priced under $100, but the preorder deal makes it sweeter. Aurzen promises a $30 discount if you prebook the upcoming projector right now for just $1. Aurzen has been dabbling with Roku TV on its projectors for quite some time. Earlier in May, it also released the first portable projector with Roku TV at the helm, and another one is confirmed to arrive shortly. This one costs less than $100, and while we’re awaiting details, Aurzen is already teasing a slight variation to the design compared to the previous model. With that, the projector maker is also promising a good discount — if you take certain steps right now. Aurzen recently opened the floor for preorders for its upcoming EAZZE E1R projector with Roku ahead of the September 1 launch. The company is letting interested folks reserve theirs by paying just $1. In exchange, these early backers will get a $30 discount voucher that they can redeem on both Aurzen’s website and Amazon.

title: Chrome on Android is falling behind — here are 5 features it needs now
summary: Google needs to do better.
body: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority Chrome on Android hasn’t kept up. That’s not a hot take — it’s just where things stand. And this is something you only realize once you step out and try other browsers like Firefox, Brave, Edge, and Samsung Internet. Extensions, proper privacy controls, customization, and background playback — competing browsers have been checking these boxes for years. The list of things Chrome still hasn’t gotten around to is longer than it should be, and it’s high time Google closed the gap.

title: One year of updates couldn’t save the Pixel 10’s GPU — and now the Pixel 11 is at risk
summary: What's the state of play with Android 17 on the Pixel 10?
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority The Pixel 10 series may be Google’s best phones yet, but gamers got the short end of the stick. The Tensor G5 marked Google’s switch away from Arm’s Mali GPUs in favor of Imagination Technologies’ PowerVR architecture — specifically the mid-range, already aging DXT-48-1536. With the Pixel 11 launch approaching, one question keeps nagging at me: will history repeat itself? Rumors suggest the Tensor G6 will use another modest PowerVR GPU, the CXTP-48-1536. If Google’s recent trajectory is anything to go by, the Pixel 11 could fall even further behind rival flagship GPUs.

title: Samsung confirms minor setback for Galaxy S26 One UI 9 beta
summary: Samsung has delayed One UI 9 beta 5 for the S26 series until next week for "final reviews and quality improvements."
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has pushed the fifth One UI 9 beta 5 update for the Galaxy S26 series to next week. The delay is due to final reviews and quality improvements to enhance system stability and fix bugs before a stable release. The over-the-air update will roll out to enrolled Galaxy S26, S26 Plus, and S26 Ultra devices in the US, UK, India, Germany, Poland, and South Korea when it goes live next week. Samsung has confirmed a short delay for the fifth beta build of One UI 9 for the Galaxy S26 series, pushing its expected release into next week. Galaxy S26 owners participating in the preview program will have to hold on a bit longer, following the rollout of the One UI 9 beta 4 update last month. According to an official announcement post on the Samsung Community forum (via Tarun Vats on X ), the development team is taking additional time for “final reviews and quality improvements” before rolling out the fifth iteration. Samsung apologized to community members for the slight delay, citing the need to deliver a more stable, polished software experience to testers.

title: Galaxy S26 FE appears at FCC with an unexpected Qualcomm twist
summary: Qualcomm and Exynos silicon in the same phone? Yep, but perhaps not in the way you're expecting.
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR We’ve uncovered the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE’s FCC filing, revealing 45W charging, reverse wireless charging, and more. The filing also mentions both Qualcomm and Samsung Exynos wireless technologies. A closer look suggests that the phone will have a Samsung modem and chipset, as well as a Qualcomm local networking chip. Samsung has just launched its new foldable phones , but we’re already looking forward to the Galaxy S26 FE ‘s imminent arrival. The phone is expected to launch in the coming weeks, and a regulatory filing has revealed a few details. The Galaxy S26 FE passed through the FCC’s database, and the filing reveals a few notable features. For one, the listing hints at both Qualcomm and Samsung Exynos silicon in the same model. Wait, what?
